text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"mkdir -p /tmp/exposed-tracking-fixture-design"}));
text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /tmp/exposed-tracking-fixture-design/a.md
+# Candidate A: opt-in worker analytics
+
+## Usage
+```ts
+// Existing entity-details and other tests: no changes.
+import { test, expect } from "./backend";
+test("entity details", async ({ page }) => { /* existing assertions */ });
+
+// search-tracking.spec.ts: add to the existing file-level test.use.
+test.use({ analytics: true, userAgent: existingChromeUserAgent });
+test("each executed search emits one event", async ({ page, backend }) => {
+  // Existing fake-host route decodes and records events before page.goto.
+});
+```
+
+## Problem
+The worker fixture unconditionally supplies fake analytics credentials, so every
+application initializes PostHog and produces cross-origin requests. Fulfilling
+those requests still exposes them to same-origin traffic assertions. The runtime
+public environment and client hook already support disabling analytics with an
+empty token or host; the fixture should express which workers need analytics.
+
+## Shape
+```ts
+type WorkerFixtures = {
+  analytics: boolean;
+  application: { url: string; backend: Backend };
+};
+export const test = base.extend<{ backend: Backend }, WorkerFixtures>({
+  analytics: [false, { option: true, scope: "worker" }],
+  application: [async ({ analytics }, use, workerInfo) => {
+    // Existing server lifecycle; child environment overrides process.env:
+    // PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN: analytics ? "phc_test_search_tracking" : ""
+    // PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST: analytics ? "https://posthog.test" : ""
+    throw new Error("not implemented");
+  }, { scope: "worker" }],
+  // Keep existing page fixture's fake-host fulfillment before yielding page.
+  // Keep baseURL and backend fixtures unchanged.
+});
+```
+`analytics` is worker scoped because application environment is immutable after
+spawn. Playwright separates incompatible worker fixture options; callers cannot
+accidentally toggle an already-running application. Always override both inherited
+environment values, including the disabled case, to avoid real credentials.
+The existing page interceptor remains unconditional and serves as a fallback;
+the tracking test's later route takes precedence and captures payloads. There is
+one public boolean because the domain has two supported test states, with no
+user-supplied host/token combinations. This hides process setup behind test.use
+and follows boundary-discipline and separate-before-serializing-shared-state.
+
+## Tradeoffs accepted
+- Accept an extra worker for analytics tests in exchange for deterministic isolation.
+- Accept a harmless default fake-host route in all tests to retain a safe fallback.
+
+## Alternatives considered
+A separately exported analyticsTest fixture hides opt-in configuration but adds a
+second entry point and fixture composition for a single boolean distinction.
+Globally enabling analytics and relaxing the traffic assertion weakens the
+existing test's same-origin contract and fails to isolate the cause.
+
+## Synthesis decision
+Pending orchestrator comparison.
+
+## Implementation reconciliation
+No implementation or repository modifications performed.
+
+## Risks and next step
+Worker options must be selected at file scope, not inside test bodies or nested
+describe groups. Add the option, run tracking and entity-details together, then
+the complete browser suite. Confirm disabled workers generate no analytics
+requests and enabled workers capture six expected search events without ingestion.
*** End Patch"));

content.text:
Wrote [candidate A](/tmp/exposed-tracking-fixture-design/a.md): typed `analytics` worker option, disabled by default and enabled through file-level `test.use` in search tracking.

Explicitly clear both PostHog environment values for disabled workers; retain fake-host interception for enabled traffic. No repository edits.
